comparison.objective: Crimp a cable lug by inserting a stripped conductor into a barrel, closing a press, then removing and returning the cable.
comparison.physical_skill: Bimanual conductor insertion and hold-while-actuating a lever; unlike the candidate, it does not mate rail and jig end faces, preserve continuous support during a regrasp, or contain free rolling elements.
comparison.success_condition: Requires specified insertion depth/alignment at crimp, lever release, extraction and return; candidate instead requires complete block transfer with every ball retained and no support-interface separation, contamination or damage.
comparison.reason: Both include alignment, insertion and bimanual coordination, but the tested outcomes differ materially: irreversible crimp formation versus continuous four-row bearing support during transfer. Candidate gap, angular and force limits are not numeric, but its ball-retention and uninterrupted-support gates establish the distinction.
